1|d3ca|  # Release notes
2|3def|  
3|43f0|  <!-- do not remove -->
4|3def|  
5|f397|  ## 0.0.1
6|3def|  
7|b410|  First release.
8|3def|  
9|ca1b|  paar is a live, lazy variable inspector for Python. It runs a small HTTP server inside your
10|bbbc|  process and shows a PyCharm-style variables pane for whatever is in the namespace, whether
11|4f8f|  that is a Jupyter kernel, a plain script, or a long training run.
12|3def|  
13|ea0b|  What you get in this release:
14|3def|  
15|942a|  - **Live view.** In IPython the pane refreshes after every cell. In any other process a
16|eb30|    background thread polls the namespace and pushes changes. You start the inspector once and
17|462b|    leave it open.
18|c779|  - **Lazy expansion.** Containers load one level at a time, on click. Opening a million-row
19|6475|    DataFrame costs nothing until you ask for it, and then only one page is read. numpy arrays
20|5f36|    and pandas frames get a scrollable, paged grid instead of a tree.
21|e224|  - **Exec, edit, filter.** Run an expression or statement against the kernel (with an isolated
22|2233|    mode that throws away side effects), click any scalar to edit it in place, and filter the
23|d5b4|    variable list by name or type. The web exec bar and the terminal both offer completion.
24|1eaf|  - **Three frontends, one server.** An inline panel in Jupyter, a full page in the browser,
25|0588|    and `paar-tui`, a Textual terminal inspector. `paar-serve script.py` runs a script under a
26|e310|    live inspector and keeps the server up afterwards so you can look at the final state.
27|5d31|  - **Many environments at once.** Each server registers itself by repo or package name in a
28|1bb6|    local registry. Any frontend can discover the running servers and switch between them, so
29|2f6a|    several projects can run paar side by side.
30|8602|  - **A restricted surface for AI agents.** `serve()` also publishes an agent API. Agent code
31|b1f8|    can read your variables and create new ones, but it writes into its own overlay layer, so
32|5822|    it can never change or delete what you made. An AST check refuses in-place mutation,
33|3c22|    `exec`/`eval` escapes, and destructive file or shell calls. Owner-only endpoints are gated
34|f69b|    by a per-server token. `paar-mcp` exposes this surface to Claude Code and Codex over stdio.
35|3def|  
36|1a09|  Install with `pip install paar`, or `pip install paar[mcp]` for the agent server.

1|9c2e|  # Design: Consolidate `nbs/` and adopt fastcore idioms
2|3def|  
3|2f31|  Date: 2026-07-23
4|fa60|  Status: Approved (design) — pending spec review
5|3def|  
6|c676|  ## Problem
7|3def|  
8|08ce|  `nbs/` has grown to 13 notebooks (+ `index.ipynb`), several of them tiny, with a
9|e91d|  real numbering bug: `08_runtime.ipynb` and `08_tui.ipynb` share the `08` prefix.
10|9d9a|  The foundation modules are small and tightly coupled (`core` 835B, `reprs` 1.1KB,
11|7cc8|  `resolvers` 3.5KB, `providers` 2.4KB, `grid` 4.8KB, `snapshot` 4.8KB), while the
12|96c7|  frontends are large (`fasthtml` 34KB, `tui` 29KB). Code predates a consistent
13|7a05|  fastcore style and tests are written as standalone test functions rather than
14|fd0c|  literate example cells.
15|3def|  
16|72da|  ## Goals
17|3def|  
18|f49e|  1. Consolidate 13 notebooks → 7 (+ `index`), grouped by dependency layer.
19|1592|  2. Fix the `08` collision via renumbering.
20|0123|  3. Rewrite code with fastcore idioms (`first`, `store_attr`, `@delegates`,
21|0603|     `@patch`, `L`, `dict2obj`) to shrink and clarify.
22|12d1|  4. Convert test cells from test-function style to nbdev **literate style**:
23|1ee7|     inline, example-driven cells interleaved with prose, with `test_eq`/asserts
24|81ab|     demonstrating usage right after each definition.
25|3def|  
26|7d70|  ## Constraints (from brainstorming)
27|3def|  
28|b606|  - **Entry-point module names must stay stable**: `paar.tui`, `paar.fasthtml`,
29|c896|    `paar.mcp` are `[project.scripts]` targets and must keep their module names.
30|9984|    Preserved via `#| default_exp` regardless of notebook filename/number.
31|64ad|  - Other module import paths **may change** (pre-1.0, v0.0.1).
32|fbe6|  - nbdev workflow: run `nbdev-prepare` (hyphen) after every notebook. Never
33|5798|    `nbdev_prepare`. hatchling build — no MANIFEST.in edits.
34|3def|  
35|19d5|  ## Target notebook layout (13 → 7 + index)
36|3def|  
37|03ec|  | New notebook        | `default_exp` | Merges (old modules)                | Rationale |
38|8dfe|  |---------------------|---------------|-------------------------------------|-----------|
39|522a|  | `00_core.ipynb`     | `core`        | core + reprs + resolvers + providers | Foundation primitives: the `VarInfo` row, value rendering, container/string dispatch registries |
40|b371|  | `01_snapshot.ipynb` | `snapshot`    | grid + snapshot                     | Data model: namespace walk + gridable slicing (grid exists only to feed snapshot) |
41|3a52|  | `02_runtime.ipynb`  | `runtime`     | runtime + bridge + registry         | Live-kernel/session layer: exec, namespace bridge, server registry |
42|1683|  | `03_agent.ipynb`    | `agent`       | agent                               | Unchanged content (imported by fasthtml) |
43|c0ef|  | `04_fasthtml.ipynb` | `fasthtml`    | fasthtml                            | Kept module name; restructured internally (see fastcore §) |
44|39af|  | `05_tui.ipynb`      | `tui`         | tui                                 | Kept module name; restructured internally |
45|47ae|  | `06_mcp.ipynb`      | `mcp`         | mcp                                 | Kept module name |
46|3def|  
47|5765|  Import paths that change (internal `from .x import` lines updated, `_modidx.py`
48|28bd|  regenerated by nbdev):
49|3def|  
50|9dac|  - `paar.reprs`, `paar.resolvers`, `paar.providers` → `paar.core`
51|e1bc|  - `paar.grid` → `paar.snapshot`
52|32de|  - `paar.bridge`, `paar.registry` → `paar.runtime`
53|3def|  
54|3f67|  Ordering respects the dependency graph (agent before fasthtml, which imports
55|245e|  `AgentSession`).
56|3def|  
57|21ed|  ## fastcore rewrite (behavior-preserving)
58|3def|  
59|f1f5|  Grounded in confirmed source patterns:
60|3def|  
61|d5b7|  - **`first`** (`fastcore.basics`) for linear "first match wins" scans:
62|61a7|    `resolve_for` (resolvers) and `provided_str` (providers).
63|4267|  - **`store_attr`** in `agent`'s `__init__` and plain (non-Textual) tui client
64|d6a7|    classes. **Skip Textual widget subclasses** unless the swap is clean —
65|c016|    Textual owns its `__init__` contract.
66|9556|  - **`@delegates`** on repeated kwarg chains: `roff,coff,rows,cols` and
67|8ea4|    `offset,limit` forwarded through bridge → snapshot → grid.
68|bd43|  - **`L`** for the list-comprehension-heavy resolver/grid children builders.
69|19df|  - **`dict2obj`/`AttrDict`** for `array_page`'s result dict — only if consumer
70|f173|    edits in fasthtml/tui stay small; otherwise leave as plain dict.
71|502f|  - **`@patch`** to split the monster `fasthtml`/`tui` classes into
72|4638|    one-method-per-cell literate cells (biggest readability win, idiomatic nbdev).
73|3def|  
74|7727|  Also centralize the repeated `try: import numpy/pandas except: None` optional
75|d68a|  imports where it doesn't create awkward cross-module coupling.
76|3def|  
77|fb2f|  ## Test cells → literate style
78|3def|  
79|91bd|  Replace blocks of standalone test functions with inline example cells:
80|3def|  
81|6b11|  - After each definition, a small cell that *uses* it on a realistic value and
82|17ed|    asserts the result with `test_eq`/`test_fail`, doubling as documentation.
83|6692|  - Prose markdown cells explaining intent between definition and example.
84|791e|  - Preserve all existing assertions' coverage — literate conversion is a
85|dde5|    reorganization, not a reduction. Net assertion count should not drop.
86|3def|  
87|29a3|  ## Execution plan
88|3def|  
89|3c2e|  - Work **one notebook at a time**, in dependency order (`00_core` first).
90|f24f|  - Apply consolidation + fastcore + literate-test conversion in the **same pass**
91|fce6|    per notebook, so each notebook is touched once.
92|32fb|  - Run `nbdev-prepare` after each notebook; require green before proceeding.
93|4b11|  - Delete superseded old notebooks only after their content lands in the new one
94|c3f2|    and tests pass.
95|4a83|  - Update `index.ipynb` cross-references and `nbs/_quarto.yml` sidebar last.
96|8e37|  - No `pyproject.toml` entry-point changes.
97|3def|  
98|95ef|  ## Risks & mitigations
99|3def|  
100|abfb|  - **`@patch`-splitting the working 34KB/29KB frontends is high churn.** Mitigate
101|02d1|    by doing frontends last, one class at a time, with `nbdev-prepare` between
102|88c1|    classes; each `@patch` cell must keep exports identical (`__all__` unchanged).
103|d73f|  - **Textual `store_attr` conflicts.** Skip where the widget base needs specific
104|0c5c|    init ordering; only convert plain data-holder classes.
105|f3c1|  - **Renumbering breaks external `import paar.reprs` etc.** Accepted at v0.0.1.
106|6d47|  - **Literate conversion could silently drop coverage.** Guard by comparing
107|d66d|    assertion counts before/after per notebook.
108|3def|  
109|46f8|  ## Success criteria
110|3def|  
111|fb82|  - 7 notebooks (+ index); no numbering collisions.
112|a729|  - `nbdev-prepare` green end to end.
113|d6eb|  - Entry points `paar-tui` / `paar-serve` / `paar-mcp` still import and run.
114|66d8|  - No net loss of test assertions.
115|48f6|  - Foundation code visibly shorter via fastcore idioms; large frontends read as
116|6048|    literate `@patch` cells.

10|4d50|  Goal: clikernel is the single persistent Python runtime an agent uses for ALL code, with paar riding inside so the owner watches/steers live, and guardrails so the agent can't clobber owner state.
11|3def|  
12|860c|  Setup (done 2026-07-23):

Editable paar means repo source edits flow through with no reinstall.
14|9154|  - `~/.config/clikernel/startup.py` runs `paar.fasthtml.serve(port=8001, name=os.environ.get('PAAR_ENV_NAME','claude'))` → paar serves the worker namespace at http://127.0.0.1:8001 (auto-bumps if taken). Watch it with `paar-tui --env claude` (resolves by name via registry ~/.paar/reg).
15|03e7|  - `~/.config/clikernel/inspectors.py` reuses `paar.agent.policy_inspectors(_owner_names)`; blocks exec/eval + fs/shell escapes always, and delete/in-place-mutation of names listed in a live `OWNER` set.
16|3def|  
17|8753|  Bug found + fixed: `paar.agent.RuleBlock` was a distinct class from `clikernel.base.RuleBlock`, so clikernel's `except RuleBlock` never caught paar inspector blocks (cell ran anyway). Fix in nbs/10_agent.ipynb cell 10-c4: `RuleBlock` now subclasses `clikernel.base.RuleBlock` when importable (falls back to Exception). See [[build-directly-small-changes]].
18|3def|  
19|3aeb|  Transport: `! clikernel` exits on EOF in Claude Code (one-shot), so it can't stay alive across turns. Stopgap this session: a broker at /tmp/ck (broker.py keeps one worker alive; write cell to /tmp/ck/req/<tok>.pending then `python3 /tmp/ck/wait.py <tok>`). The seamless replacement is registering `clikernel-mcp` as an MCP server (native execute/restart/interrupt tools, persistent, no broker) — set PAAR_ENV_NAME=claude in its config.

15|03e7|  - `~/.config/clikernel/inspectors.py` reuses `paar.agent.policy_inspectors(_owner_names)`; blocks exec/eval + fs/shell escapes always, and delete/in-place-mutation of names listed in a live `OWNER` set.
16|3def|  
17|8753|  Bug found + fixed: `paar.agent.RuleBlock` was a distinct class from `clikernel.base.RuleBlock`, so clikernel's `except RuleBlock` never caught paar inspector blocks (cell ran anyway). 19|95ab|  Transport: `! clikernel` exits on EOF in Claude Code (one-shot). Broker stopgap at /tmp/ck. MCP registration is disabled by admin, so `claude mcp add clikernel-mcp` is out.

21|73e9|  PRODUCTIZED (2026-07-23): paar now owns the agent runtime. `clikernel` is a core dep. New module `paar/kernel.py` (nbs/12_kernel.ipynb): `AgentKernel` supervises a persistent clikernel worker in paar's own interpreter (`sys.executable -m clikernel.cli`); `guarded_run` applies `policy_inspectors` at the paar layer BEFORE forwarding. `serve()`/`inspector()` gained `agent_kernel=True` (default) which auto-starts the worker and has it ride its own paar env (`<env>-agent`). New additive endpoints `/kernel/api/exec` + `/kernel/api/info` (the `/agent/api` overlay + `paar-mcp` were left untouched, per request — for other devs). New CLI `paar-exec [--env|--url] CODE` posts to `/kernel/api/exec`. True isolation verified: worker is a separate pid, owner vars invisible to it, escapes blocked. RECURSION GUARD is critical: worker startup runs `serve()` which would re-spawn a kernel → fork bomb; `AgentKernel` sets env `PAAR_AGENT_WORKER=1` and `_ensure_kernel()` no-ops when it's set.
